newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian sell-off agency gets new chief supervisor. [CORRECTED 17:46 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian sell-off agency gets new chief supervisor. [CORRECTED 17:46 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline by adding dropped word "supervisor", to make clear new appointee is head of supervisory body, not of privatisation agency itself.)
Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency (PA) supervisory board on Tuesday elected as chairman Yosif Iliev, current head of the government Tender Committee, state news agency BTA said.
The function of the supervisory board is to approve each privatisation deal.
A new seven-member supervisory board was appointed on Monday after the previous supervisory board resigned in September over disagreements with the Socialist government.
One of the first tasks of the board is to approve a deal signed on December 19 with Belgian chemicals company Solvay SA for the acquisition of 60 percent of soda ash producer Sodi for $160 million.
Bulgaria completed privatisation deals worth 95.93 billion levs for 509 enterprises in 1996 and plans to concentrate on fewer, higher-value deals in 1997, the privatisation agency said in December.
